prompt: Our notification service fronts every send with a per-recipient rate limiter running on a Redis Cluster: it caps how many push/email/SMS notifications a given user can receive per channel per window. Here's the current `RateLimiterService` implementation — it passes every load test we throw at aggregate traffic, but the moment a single user goes "viral" (a broadcast fan-out hammering one user×channel pair), that one recipient's traffic saturates a single Redis Cluster node while the rest of the cluster sits idle. Walk me through why this specific implementation causes that, then optimize the code so the same aggregate per-user limit is enforced but the load no longer concentrates on one shard.
